index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure is divided into three main parts labeled (a), (b), and (c), each illustrating different aspects of a proposed framework for cross-lingual caption refinement (CCR). 

Part (a) demonstrates the variability in textual expression for the same image content. On the left, an image shows a cat sitting on a cobblestone ground. Three Chinese captions are provided, each with an English translation in parentheses: '地上坐着一只猫。' (On the ground sitting a cat.), '一只猫坐在鹅卵石地面上。' (A cat sitting on the cobblestone ground.), and '鹅卵石地面上有一只猫。' (On cobblestone ground there is a cat.). Each caption is linked via dashed blue arrows to the image. To the right, under the heading 'Expressions', colored rectangular boxes represent semantic components extracted from each caption: Location (yellow), Action (orange), Agent (blue), Object (green). The first caption yields Location, Action, Agent; the second yields Agent, Action, Object; and the third yields Location, Object. This illustrates that different linguistic expressions can convey the same underlying semantics.

Part (b) presents a typical adapter setup for target-language encoding. A dashed blue box labeled 'Target-Language Caption' contains the Chinese text '一只猫坐在鹅卵石地面上.' This input feeds into a light green rounded rectangle labeled 'Pretrained Text Encoder', which has a blue snowflake icon indicating it is frozen (not trainable). The output of this encoder is added to a peach-colored square labeled 'A' with a red flame icon, signifying it is trainable. The result is passed through a solid blue vertical bar, representing the final encoded output. This section highlights the standard approach where a fixed adapter is applied to a frozen pretrained model.

Part (c) introduces the proposed DASD framework for CCR. Again, the input is a 'Target-Language Caption' in a dashed blue box with the same Chinese text. This input is processed by a tall blue rectangle labeled 'Semantics Disentangling'. This module splits the caption into two streams: 'Semantic-related Features' (in a dashed gray box containing examples like 'key actions, event participants ...') and 'Semantic-agnostic Features' (in a dashed light blue box with examples like 'caption length, way of expression ...'). The 'Semantic-related Features' are fed into a 'Pretrained Text Encoder' (light green, with a blue snowflake icon, indicating it is frozen). The output of this encoder is then added to a peach-colored square labeled 'DA' (Dynamic Adapter), marked with a red flame icon, indicating it is trainable. The 'Semantic-agnostic Features' are also connected to the DA module, suggesting they influence its parameters dynamically. The combined output passes through a solid blue vertical bar, similar to part (b). A legend on the right clarifies the icons: a blue snowflake means 'Frozen' and a red flame means 'Trainable'. This structure emphasizes that the proposed method dynamically adapts based on both semantic and non-semantic characteristics of the input caption.
